text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Prime Minister Netanyahu says justice minister misled him by recommending Bar-On as attorney-general.
- Jerusalem mayor says Netanyahu told him Har Homa building project will be approved this week.
- M.I. Holdings to ask finance minister today to publish new tender for sale of Bank Hapoalim.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- "Netanyahu effect" depresses Tel Aviv stock prices.
- Bosch considering establishing research and development facility in Israel.
- Bank of Israel to announce March interest rates today.
MAARIV
- Treasury's budget director says Bank of Israel rates policy will increase budget this year by about four billion shekels.
- Tourism ministry to invest about $5 million in developing tourism in Jewish settlements.
- Israel Aircraft Industries negotiating sale of satellites to several countries.
GLOBES

- Senior economic officials in Jerusalem estimate that political crisis over appointment of attorney-general could deepen economic crisis and hurt investment, privatisation and ability to attract foreign capital.
- Bank of Israel governor Frenkel expected to lower interest rate today by 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point.
- Head of Israeli Securities Authority says no signs current stock market revival signals end of capital markets crisis.
- Shamrock in preliminary contacts with Fox, Universal and CBS on selling its 23 percent stake in Telad, which holds Israeli Channel Two concession.
JERUSALEM POST
- State Attorney, police push for lid on leaks in investigation of Bar-On affair.
- Netanyahu pledges Har Homa quid pro quo.
- Turkmenis seek to supply gas to Israel.
